basis: jinshu:053:s0002–s0013 identifies 武帝 as Minhuai’s grandfather and Hui’s predecessor; source106 assigns the pigpen emperor to p004. Funeral quotations s0131–s0148 distinguish Hui as current speaker from the cited 先帝/聖祖, and the historian’s 武皇/皇祖 references repeat that grandfather. This defines the central Western Jin Wu identity.

The explicit accession and era anchors connect the external Jin records: jinshu:024:s0206/s0211 晉受命，武帝 and s0226 咸甯四年; jinshu:037 repeated 武帝受禪 after Wei offices and before Taishi domain dates; jinshu:094:s0145 武帝踐阼，泰始中; jinshu:028:s0054 武帝字安世. These specific contexts establish the same founder, rather than merging on a reused Wu title alone.

All27 full current members are assessed individually in member-assessments.json with current primary unit citations, quoted/anaphoric frames and family/era distinctions. The source supports one transitive27-member merge covering all26 owned current canonical pairs. No canonical ID is pinned or aliases invented.

Later memorials are retrospective: jinshu:020:s0443–s0445 quotes the earlier 武皇帝詔 during An’s Yuanxing1 reign; jiutangshu:084:s0299 explicitly says 晉武 in a Tang argument; jinshu:111:s0230 uses Wu’s Taikang as an older dating reference. These references do not move Wu into the later narrative era.
